quote: subjects instructed to avoid anchoring still seem to do so
content: Replication check: the unpublished Quattrone manuscript cannot be checked directly, but its claim that warnings do not prevent anchoring has been tested repeatedly and holds. Wilson, Houston, Etling & Brekke (1996) found that explicitly forewarning participants about anchoring did not reduce it, and three large replications (Röseler et al. 2024, about 650 participants) again found no effect of forewarning, cognitive load or need for cognition on anchoring. This is one of the claims in the essay that has become better supported over time.
